_FLOW: GLOBAL DOI COHORT CENSUS — the Platform Erosion Observatory's scale instrument. The observatory's purpose is global DOI erasure, not one archive's deletions, and until this file it had no instrument operating at global scale. THE MEASUREMENT PRINCIPLE: a publication-year cohort's DOI count should be MONOTONICALLY NON-DECREASING. New DOIs can be minted with a past publication year, so a cohort may grow; existing DOIs should not vanish from the index. ANY DECREASE IS AN ERASURE EVENT, and it is detectable at one API call per cohort.
method: One count per publication-year cohort, 1990-2026. Public API, declared user agent, no authentication. 37 calls per epoch. The instrument is cheap enough to run monthly and simple enough that anyone can reproduce it.
unaccounted_note: 5.3M DOIs carry no publicationYear in 1990-2026 — future-dated, absent, or malformed. They are outside cohort coverage and a full-coverage instrument would need a second key.
baseline_status: FIRST EPOCH. No comparison is possible from one point. Every number here is a baseline against which the next epoch is diffed, and no erosion claim can be made until a second epoch exists.
what_a_decrease_means: A cohort count lower than a prior epoch means DOIs left the DataCite index between epochs. That is not necessarily deletion — a DOI moving from findable to registered state leaves the public index while continuing to resolve. Distinguishing withdrawal-from-findability from full deregistration requires a second query per affected cohort and is NOT part of this instrument as specified.
known_limits: publicationYear is metadata and can be edited; a cohort could shrink because DOIs were re-dated rather than erased. A shrinking cohort adjacent to a growing one is the signature and must be checked before any erasure claim.
The API total and the cohort sum are computed from different queries and may diverge for reasons unrelated to erasure.
One epoch establishes nothing. This file's entire value is as a fixed point.
